FOREWORD

This Indian Standard which is identical with IS0 8892 : 1987 `Oilseed residues - Determination of total residual hexane' issued by the international Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ), was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 25 March 1990 on the recommendation of the Nutrition Sectional Committee ( FAD 21 ) and approval of the Food and Agriculture Division Council. The text of IS0 standard has been approved as suitable for publication as Indian Standard without deviations. Certain conventions are however not. identical to those used in Indian Standards, attention is especially drawn to the following : a) Wherever the words `International Standard' appear, referring to this standard, they should be read as' Indian Standard'; b) Comma ( , ) has been used as a decimal marker while in Indian Standards, the current practice is to use a point ( . ) as the decimal marker; and c) Wherever cross references appear in the text, only the corresponding Indian Standard shall be followed. CROSS REFERENCES ln this Indian Standard, the following International Standard is referred to: IS0 5500 Oilseed residues Sampling

The technical committee responsible for the preparation of this standard has reviewed the provisions of the above mentioned IS0 standard and has decided that it is acceptable for use in conjunction with this standard.

1

Scope and field of application

This International Standard specifies a method for the determination of the total amount of volatile hydrocarbons, referred to generally as hexane, remaining in oilsaed residues after extraction with hydrocarbon-based solvents.

If a capillary column is used, the apparatus shall have a 1/ 100 input divider.

IS0 5590, Oilseed residues -

3

principle

Desorption of hexane by heating at 110 "C with water in a closed vessel, and determination of the hexane in the headspace by gas chromatography using capillary or packed columns. Expression of the results as n-hexane.

Penicillin-type flasks, of capacity 50 to 50 ml, all with 5.4 the same volume to within 2 %. 5.5 Septa, inert to solvents, of approximately 3 mm thickness, of a material such as nitrile rubber (for example Perbunan), or butyl rubber with a PTFE or polychloroprene seam (for example Neoprene).
NOTE -- Ensure that the septa used will produce a hermetic seal after crimping.

4

Reagents and materials

4.1 Technical n-hexane or light petroleum, with a composition similar to that used in the industrial extraction of oilseeds, or failing that, n-hexane. 4.2 Carrier gas : hydrogen or nitrogen, helium, etc., dry and containing less than 10 mg/kg of oxygen. 4.3 Auxiliary gases : Hydrogen, 99,9 % pure, containing no organic impurities, Air, containing no organic impurities.

5.6 5.7 5.8

Metallic

foil caps, for example of aluminium.

Crimping pliers. Liquid syringe, of capacity 10 ul.

6

Sampling

and sample storage

See IS0 5500. It is essential that loss of hexane from the sample be prevented. The laboratory sample shall fill a completely sealed container (preferably a crimped metal box) and shall be stored at - 20 OC or below (for example in a deep-freezer). Plastics containers shall not be used. The determination of residual hexane shall be carried out as soon as the container has been brought to room temperature and opened. .

5

Apparatus

Usual laboratory apparatus and in particular 5.1 Gas chromatograph, with flame ionization detector and integrator and/or recorder, equipped with a glass capillary column approrimately 30 m long and 0.3 mm in diameter, coated

remove the flasks from the oven and leave to cool for 2 min. With the gas syringe heated to between 50 and 60 OC, take exactly 0.5 ml of the headspace and inject quickly into the chromatograph.

Weigh, ;o the nearest 0, t g, 5 g of the laboratory sample into a flask (5.4). Add 2,5 ml of distilled water, seal the flask with a septum (5.51, cover with a foil cap (5.6) and crimp with the pliers (5.7). All these operations shall be performed rapidly.

7.4

Number

of determinations

Carry out two determinations on the same laboratory sample.

8
7.2

Expression of results

Desorption

of the hexane
Construct the calibration graph by plotting the area of the sol- 1 vent peak as a function of the mass of solvent introduced into 1 the flask (1 pi corresponding to 660 pg). Determine the sum of the peak areas of the hexane and various hydrocarbons which usually make up the technical solvent (Zmethyl pentane, 3-methyl pentane, methylcyclopentane, cyclohexane, etc.).
NOTE - Do not include peaks due to oxidation products if present in significant amounts, but report these separately.

Place the flask in the oven (5.21, maintained at 110 "C, for 90 min. When this time has elapsed, remove the flask from the oven and leave to cool for 2 min. then agitate by inverting.
NOTE - It is important to leave the flasks in the oven for the same length of time for each sample.

9

Precision

Three points, for example with 2, 5 and 10 pl of solvent, are usually sufficient for constructing the calibration graph; they correspond to 264, 660 and 1 320 mg/kg of hexane if the test portion is 5 g of residue. Prepare a calibration series using flasks (5.4) of the same capacity as those used for the determination. Add to the flasks 6 ml of water'), followed immediately by various quantities of n-hexane (4.1). measured accurately with the aid of the syringe (5.8). Seal each flask with & septum (5.51, cover with a foil cap 15.6) and crimp with the pliers (5.7). Place the various flasks for the establishment of one calibration graph in the oven for 15 min at 110 OC. At the end of this time,

Two interlaboratory tests organized at the international level with 12 laboratories participating, each carrying out three determinations (No. 11, and 15 laboratories, each carrying out two determinations (No. 21, gave the statistical results (determined in accordance with IS0 5725) shown in the table.

10

Test report

The test report shall show the method usad and the results obtained. It shall also mention any operating details not specified in this International Standard, or regarded as optional, together with details of any incidents likely to have influenced the results. The report shall include all the information necessary for the complete identification of the sample. *
